title: Building an Emergency Cushion
summary: Why an emergency reserve protects your daily plan and prevents high-interest borrowing.

quiz.question: If an unexpected expense of €250 arises and you have a €500 emergency buffer, what is the safest next step?
options: Borrow money from a high-interest credit card to keep the cushion untouched
Use €250 from your buffer for the expense, then gradually replenish it when possible
Ignore the expense and skip upcoming scheduled bills
quiz.explanation: An emergency cushion is specifically designed to absorb unexpected necessary costs without relying on high-interest debt. After using it, the recommended action is to replenish the cushion gradually when cash flow allows.

title: Liquidity Buffer vs Long-Term Savings
summary: Understanding the difference between money kept in your checking account for upcoming bills and true savings.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining a liquidity buffer in your day-to-day checking account?
options: To earn the highest long-term interest rate on your money
To absorb billing timing mismatches and prevent accidental overdrafts before payday
To lock money away so that it can never be accessed for bills
quiz.explanation: A liquidity buffer provides immediate breathing room in your checking account, absorbing temporary timing differences between outgoing debits and incoming salary without fees.

title: APR and the True Cost of Minimum Payments
summary: How annual interest rates compound and why paying only the minimum prolongs debt.

quiz.question: What happens when you pay more than the required minimum payment on a loan or credit card?
options: The extra payment is held by the bank as an administrative penalty
The extra amount reduces the principal directly, reducing future interest charges
Your interest rate is automatically increased by the lender
quiz.explanation: Any payment above the minimum goes directly toward reducing the loan's principal balance, which immediately shrinks the baseline on which next month's interest is calculated.

title: Debt Payoff: Avalanche vs Snowball
summary: Comparing the two most effective deterministic repayment strategies to choose what works best for you.

quiz.question: Which debt repayment strategy is mathematically optimal for minimizing total interest paid?
options: Debt Avalanche (targeting the debt with the highest APR first)
Debt Snowball (targeting the debt with the smallest balance first)
Paying random amounts across all accounts with no set priority
quiz.explanation: The Avalanche method focuses all extra repayment capacity on the highest interest rate first, which mathematically saves the most money in total interest charges over time.

title: Budgeting with Irregular or Variable Income
summary: Practical rules for planning spending when your pay varies from month to month.

quiz.question: What is the recommended strategy when you experience a higher-than-average income month on variable earnings?
options: Immediately lock all surplus money into illiquid multi-year investments
Deposit the surplus into an income holding buffer to smooth future lower-income months
Increase ongoing fixed recurring commitments to match that month's earnings
quiz.explanation: Channeling surplus from strong months into an accessible holding buffer ensures you have funds ready to cover non-negotiable bills during slower months without stress.

title: Auditing Subscriptions and Recurring Charges
summary: How small recurring debits quietly erode cash flow and how to review them calmly.

quiz.question: What is the most effective approach to handling recurring subscriptions you haven't used recently?
options: Keep paying in case you might want to use them six months from now
Cancel or pause them, knowing you can easily reactivate if genuinely needed later
Ignore bank statements to avoid making decisions
quiz.explanation: Canceling inactive subscriptions immediately stops cash leakage with zero long-term penalty, as virtually all modern digital services allow instant reactivation.

title: Structuring Realistic Savings Goals
summary: Breaking targets into sustainable milestones without suffocating daily life.

quiz.question: If your monthly living costs increase, what is the recommended way to handle an active savings goal?
options: Skip paying utility bills to keep your savings target unchanged
Adjust the monthly contribution or extend the goal target date to keep cash flow safe
Take out a personal loan to hit the savings deadline
quiz.explanation: Savings goals should adapt to real-world cash flow changes. Extending the timeline or reducing monthly contributions preserves financial stability without derailing the goal entirely.

title: Navigating a Cash Shortfall and Seeking Help
summary: Objective, calm steps to take when upcoming obligations exceed available cash.

quiz.question: What is the critical first action when an upcoming cash shortfall is identified?
options: Continue funding optional discretionary savings goals as normal
Pause optional allocations and triage essential survival bills (rent, food, heat)
Borrow from unregulated high-interest payday lenders
quiz.explanation: In a shortfall, immediately pausing non-essential allocations protects available cash for non-negotiable living needs while you arrange payment plans or seek qualified external help.

title: How to Read and Reconcile Bank Statements
summary: Decoding transaction dates, pending authorizations, and statement balances.

quiz.question: Why might your bank account's available balance be lower than your posted balance?
options: The bank made an irreversible accounting error
Pending card authorizations have been reserved by merchants but not yet settled
Future salary deposits have already been credited early
quiz.explanation: Pending authorizations immediately reduce your available spending capacity so that funds are reserved until the merchant finalizes settlement, preventing overdrafts.

title: Planned Steps vs Real Transfers
summary: Why creating a step in your plan does not automatically move money.

quiz.question: When you accept a savings recommendation in FinAgent, what happens to your real bank account?
options: FinAgent automatically debits your bank account via direct debit
Nothing; it records a planned reservation in the app until you make the transfer yourself
Your money is locked by the government
quiz.explanation: FinAgent never initiates transactions or moves money. Accepting an action records a planned reservation within the app, which you execute in your real bank account when ready.
